grh_921b325b519d83c3bff5.title: Ivy
paragraphs: Ambitious Ivy Lexton wants a richer life than her husband Jim can provide and secretly carries on with doctor Roger Gretorex while setting her sights on millionaire Miles Rushworth. She steals poison from Roger's dispensary and murders Jim, allowing suspicion to fall on Roger, who confesses rather than expose the woman he loves. As Roger's execution approaches, a witness finally admits seeing Ivy take the poison and the police uncover both motive and evidence. Roger is reprieved, Miles rejects Ivy after learning what the police know, and the fortune-teller's prophecy that has haunted Ivy closes in on her. With nowhere left to run, Ivy calls Detective Lieutenant Martin and says she will be waiting for him.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Joan Fontaine, Charles Drake, Ken Christy, [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]], and Noreen Gammill. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Howard Wiley as producer, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 60 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.2c66c6e3c7434656|Ivy]].

grh_92c82ddf987fcf470e60.title: The Prince of Pilsen
paragraphs: Prince Carl Otto of Pilsen spends his Heidelberg spring vacation in southern France and discovers that an American brewer from Cincinnati has been mistaken for him by the hotel and townspeople. The confusion lets Carl meet the brewer's daughter and fall in love with her while the supposed prince enjoys royal treatment and becomes entangled in threats intended for the real prince. paragraphs: A mysterious passenger from the Star of Bermuda sends Shayne a $100 bill through an intermediary, beginning a chain of unusually generous payments, stolen identification and murder. paragraphs: Gene opens with 'Old Time Religion' before a story about ranchers being squeezed by Cody Bennett, who controls a crucial water source and charges excessive prices.
